title: Is There a Causal Relation between Maternal Acetaminophen Administration and ADHD?
ehr_evidence: Pregnant CD1 mice (N = 8/group) were allocated to receive by gavage either APAP (150 mg/kg/day, equivalent to the FDA-approved maximum human clinical dose), or 0.5% carboxymethylcellulose (control group), starting on embryonic day 7 until delivery.
summary: Preclinical experimental study investigating whether prenatal acetaminophen exposure causes hyperkinetic dysfunction/ADHD-like behavior in mouse offspring using behavioral, MRI, and histological assessments.
key_findings: Maternal serum APAP concentration peaked at 30 min after gavage, reaching a mean of 117 μg/ml.
No significant differences in maternal serum ALT concentrations between groups (P = 0.3 and P = 0.5).
No significant differences in locomotor activity parameters between groups (all P > 0.008).
No significant differences in volumes of 29 brain areas on MRI or neuronal quantification between groups.
population: pregnant CD1 mice and postnatal day 30 offspring
limitations: lack of established animal model for ADHD
oral gavage may act as a stressor
absence of 24hr home cage activity monitoring
narrow focus on hyperkinetic behavior only
intervention limited to pregnancy without lactation period
data_availability_statement: All relevant data are within the paper and its Supporting Information files.
